whatItIs.text: A pseudocereal — kin to spinach and amaranth, not a grass — grown for protein-rich seeds; its name comes from the Quechua kinwa.

historyNote.text: Quinoa was first grown in the Andes to feed livestock 5,200-7,000 years ago and entered human diets 3,000-4,000 years ago around Lake Titicaca; global demand tripled its price between 2006 and 2014, a boom-and-bust that reshaped Andean farming.

howToChoose.text: Choose seeds that smell fresh and grassy (they keep longer than the date suggests if stored cool); pre-rinsed varieties save a step, otherwise rinse well to lift the bitter saponin coating.

storage.text: Keep dry and airtight in a cool cupboard. The rulebook has the details.
storage.note: dry-goods storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Cooked quinoa chills into salads, crisps into patties with egg, or fills peppers; it freezes well flat in bags, which solves the always-too-much problem.
